title: Non-interventional Study with Ozawade® in patients with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome
summary:
The drug Ozawade® examined here has been approved on the German market since November 2021. Ozawade® is intended for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness in patients diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) whose excessive daytime sleepiness has not been satisfactorily controlled by primary OSA therapy, such as CPAP (continuous positive airway pressure) ventilation, or when a such therapy was not tolerated.
The study conducted here will collect additional data on the efficacy and safety of Ozawade® when the drug is used as an adjunctive therapy to standard care in patients with obstructive sleep apnea in order to then scientifically evaluate it.
This helps to increase knowledge about the treatment and contribute to improving treatment in the future.
Additional investigations are not carried out. It is only about the collection of data in your routine treatment.

interventions.name:
Observation group: Patients diagnosed with OSA and residual excessive daytime sleepiness despite current or prior OSA treatment. Ozawade® is prescribed independently of the study and in accordance with its SmPC.

3 Visits: Baseline, 12-weeks-FU; 24-weeks FU
- Baseline: demographics, cardiovascula

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- OSA diagnosis according to the International Classification of Sleep Disorders 3rd Edition criteria
- Residual excessive daytime sleepiness with ESS >=12
despite treatment, or after CPAP treatment attempt (or alternative OSA treatment attempt)
- new treatment with Ozawade® (patient is treatment naïve to wake-promoting pharmacotherapy)
- Signed informed consent by the patient Exclusion criteri
Exclusion criteria:
Patient is unable to understand the informed consent form.
